# PSD fixture provenance

`2layers.psd` and `transparentbg-gimp.psd` are unchanged copies of the small raster test fixtures in [psd-tools/psd-tools](https://github.com/psd-tools/psd-tools/tree/b1b454baa5fdc4d72e26b9b4bd29b2e8ad1fb93b/tests/psd_files), pinned at commit `b1b454baa5fdc4d72e26b9b4bd29b2e8ad1fb93b`. The repository's MIT license (copyright 2019 Kota Yamaguchi) is retained in `LICENSE`. They contain simple green raster test marks, not user assets. These exercise actual third-party/GIMP-written PSD bytes and Unicode names; they do not establish general Photoshop fidelity.

`seecut-layered.psd` is an original SeeCut synthetic PSD v1 fixture, generated by `psd::tests::write_synthetic`: 8×6 RGB canvas; three raster layers, two nested isolated groups; UTF-16 Chinese names; a partially off-canvas raster and relative-position bitmap mask; a hidden, partially opaque Multiply layer. Its merged-image placeholder is black, so its oracle is the explicit layer assertions, **not** its merged preview. This fixture is AGPL-3.0-or-later like its test generator. No production PSD writer is provided.

Recreate only the synthetic fixture by running the core test binary with `SEECUT_PSD_SYNTHETIC=<output path>` and `psd::tests::write_synthetic --exact --ignored`.
